# rework claims, round 3 (policy-task audit revision_2)

- CG2-E1 → The earliest-sale-date clauses carried by the sale-notice policy (its two overwrites and the matching rule sentences) now define one record test. The earliest sale date is the latest deadline_date among the case's notices whose own deadline_date falls at least the class minimum after their own activity_date. A notice that fails that test never sets or moves the date, whether it was mailed before, after or on the same day as another notice; while no such notice exists, no sale date runs. Probed for compliant-then-short, short-then-compliant, same-day and tied-date sequences (plan.md).
- CG2-E1 related (O2-1) → The redemption payment's prerequisite sentence and condition now say the latest stated earliest sale date must be carried by at least one compliant notice. This leaves one reading when two notices state the same date.
- CG2-Q1 (a) → The reinstatement payment no longer claims a quote's expense portion. Its overwrite now retires the base settlement clause, so the borrower's own payment settles the expenses through the payment date. A quote keeps stating base expenses through its own good-through date at the class storage rate. No rule borrows the payment-date grace test for a quote.
- CG2-Q1 (b) → The sibling storage sentence in both payment rules (rule text and overwrite) is self-contained. Each borrower payment uses the storage rules of its own payment rule. Storage posted on release or sale, and storage in a quote's expenses, use the class daily rate.
- CG2-Q1 (c) → The sale-notice stated amount has its own formula keyed to the notice's mailing date: installments due through the mailing date less partial credit, plus fees due, plus expenses posted on or before the mailing date, plus storage at the class rate. It is declared as an overwrite of the base "reinstatement amount where reinstatement is available" clause.
- CG2-Q1 class sweep → No other rule defines a figure as another policy computes it. The remaining cross-rule mentions are scope statements naming sibling cases (fee/surrender tails, settlement tails), as XF 20 requires.
- T0-R2-S1 → Every seeded row of task 0's 2025 case was re-checked against the current rules as of its own date: cure notice, agency fee, transport, notice of intent to sell, borrower expense payment. The notice's stated amount was re-priced by the new mailing-date formula, since reinstatement was then available. The seed-consistency entry and design_rationale SEED sentence now state the derivation.
- Task 1 → World and scored figures unchanged. Only the seeded notice's non-scored stated amount was re-priced under the new mailing-date formula (forced by CG2-Q1 (c)), and the matching proof text was updated.
